subject: NeuroSync: chat streaming idle disconnects → retry flood / exec escalation
summary: Customer production observed elevated 5xx/429 and client-side streaming timeouts leading to aggressive client retries. Immediate mitigation and exec briefing requested; mitigation included temporary throttling and routing fallback. Incident postmortem and credit request pending.
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex@neurosync.health>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: NeuroSync: chat streaming idle disconnects → retry flood

Alex —

We just saw your support ticket come through and the spike in 5xx/429 from our side. Thank you for flagging. From the Redwood console it looks like a surge of short-lived streaming connections from your client (many ended with client-side timeouts), then a burst of retries that pushed concurrent streams over the customer's routing shard and produced transient 5xx/429 responses.

Can you confirm: 1) exact client SDK version & timeout settings, 2) whether your client is using exponential backoff or fixed interval retries, and 3) whether the stream sessions have a keepalive/heartbeat? That info will help us triage quickly.

Attaching a trimmed sample of the request payloads we see and a short timeline. I’ve looped in Jonas (SRE) and Marissa (CS) for immediate support. If the symptoms are affecting users now, we should stand up a short bridge — please let me know availability.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: neurosync_request_sample.json (json), slo-incident-timeline.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Turner <alex@neurosync.health>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@neurosync.health, Chris Lang <chris.lang@neurosync.health>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeuroSync: chat streaming idle disconnects → retry flood

Thanks Vivek — quick answers inline.

- SDK: ns-chat-sdk v2.3.1 (we shipped that last week)
- Timeouts: we set a client-side stream timeout of 8s (to surface no-response quickly)
- Retries: simple fixed retry of 1s, 3 attempts (we thought that would be gentle)
- Heartbeat: none today — client opens stream, waits for messages and times out after 8s

We saw the exact symptom you described: many sockets close at ~8s, then clients immediately retry en masse. Our ops team started disabling some background workers but this is still impacting a subset of users (web clients primarily).

We’re available for a quick bridge now. Also open to a temporary suggestion from your side for a mitigation we can flip ASAP.

— Alex
Director of Platform, NeuroSync Health
alex@neurosync.health

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex@neurosync.health>, ops-team@neurosync.health
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeuroSync: chat streaming idle disconnects → retry flood

Alex / Vivek —

I pulled the live traces and logs. Root cause summary: a pattern of short-lived client timeouts (8s) where the model was still generating (typical generation times for some long-turn prompts are 12–14s). When the client disconnects the stream we see a cascade: client-side disconnect triggers server-side abort, our router immediately frees the worker but the client retries immediately with the same concurrency window, which causes a sharp increase in queued requests and upstream 5xx/429 when worker pools exhaust.

Immediate mitigations I recommend we flip now (low risk):
- Have NeuroSync increase client-side timeout to 25s for streaming requests (prevents premature disconnects).
- Set client retry backoff to exponential starting at 500ms (jittered) with max 5s (avoid fixed 1s).
- From Redwood side: temporarily drop concurrent stream limit per source by 20% for that account and enable fallback to a smaller model variant when queue depth > threshold. This should reduce burst pressure.

I can push the temporary routing/limit change now if you give me an ACK. I’ll also open tracing hooks to capture per-connection sequence numbers so we can correlate aborts -> retries.

-Jonas
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: live-logs-trimmed.txt

From: Alex Turner <alex@neurosync.health>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@neurosync.health
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeuroSync: chat streaming idle disconnects → retry flood

Jonas — thanks, that aligns with our observations. Please apply the routing/concurrency change. We’ll push a client patch with the increased timeout and exponential backoff — estimate 30 minutes for a staged rollout to web clients.

We appreciate the quick turnaround. If this reduces 5xx/429 we’ll consider this closed; if not, we’ll need a longer bridge and exec alignment.

— Alex

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: URGENT: NeuroSync production impact — asking for exec visibility and credit discussion

Marissa / Grace / Hannah —

Quick update: NeuroSync reported user-facing errors tied to the stream retry storm described above. Jonas has applied a temporary routing cap and fallback to a smaller variant while their client patch rolls out. Alex expects the client-side change to reach majority of web clients within ~30 minutes. We are currently seeing a decline in 5xx rates but want to preempt executive escalation.

Requests: 1) Can we queue a 30-min exec sync with NeuroSync if errors don’t return to baseline by 11:30 PT? 2) Please prepare the standard credit options (SLA exception + usage credit ranges) and the incident timeline PDF (I attached a trimmed copy to the initial message). 3) CS: please make the renewal lead aware if this escalates.

I’ll stay on the thread and keep you posted.

Best,
Vivek

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex@neurosync.health>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: NeuroSync production impact — asking for exec visibility and credit discussion

Thanks Vivek — good containment work. Update from CS: NeuroSync reports error rate back to near baseline after the client rollout and the routing cap. They did request an SLA credit conversation; I’ve prepared two options: 5% usage credit (standard) or 10% + case-level service review (for sustained impact). I’ve attached suggested language for outreach and a draft exec talking points doc in the shared drive link.

If Alex is comfortable we can close the incident and open a follow-up postmortem to finalize mitigation changes (heartbeat guidance + SDK recommendations). I’ll coordinate with Growth on renewal communications if that becomes necessary.

— Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
